intro_seen.description: Player has seen the waking-on-the-beach narration.

shingle_met_pell.description: Player has met Pell on Shingle Point.

saltmarrow_met_mara.description: Player has met Mara Tollen, the harbormaster.

saltmarrow_mara_told_of_dunstan.description: Mara told the player her brother Dunstan walked into the fog.

saltmarrow_met_aldous.description: Player has met Brother Aldous Wren.

saltmarrow_pebble_fate.description: What the player did with the humming pebble Remnant: '' (not decided), 'given' (to Pell) or 'kept'. Pays off when the Gull's Beacon needs a memory to burn.

saltmarrow_aldous_approach.description: How the player first handled Aldous's evasions: '' / 'gentle' / 'pressed'. Gentle earns his trust (he confides sooner in Act I); pressed makes him defensive.

saltmarrow_hesk_saw_dunstan.description: Old Hesk, Hushed in the net-lofts, told the player a big man with a lantern and 'Tollen shoulders' went north laughing, saying he'd come back for his name.

saltmarrow_mara_knows_dunstan_chose.description: Player told Mara what Hesk saw: Dunstan went into the fog willingly. Pays off when Dunstan is found among the Unmoored (Act II).

saltmarrow_pell_lent_pebble.description: Pell agreed to hand the humming pebble back so the Gull's Beacon could burn it. Stays true even if the player later returns it.

saltmarrow_mara_offered_gull.description: Mara held Dunstan's whittled gull in the fog until it became a Remnant of her memory of him, and gave it to the player for the beacon.

saltmarrow_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Gull's Beacon: '' (unlit), 'pebble' (the lullaby — Mara's song, Pell's comfort), 'knot' (Saltmarrow's founding knot) or 'gull' (Mara's memory of her brother Dunstan). The Act I choice; Saltmarrow forgets it for good.

saltmarrow_mara_saw_beacon_lit.description: Player has spoken with Mara after the Gull's Beacon was relit (one-time aftermath scene).

saltmarrow_aldous_balked.description: After the beacon was lit, a player who had not been gentle with Aldous asked for his story; he refused and sent them away. Unlocks showing him the ember on the next visit.

saltmarrow_aldous_novice.description: Asked Aldous about the novice on the east stair (Day 47, The East Stair; needs thornwold_lamp_name=told): '' (not yet), 'lamp' (asked for Wynn's sake: he sends his sorry) or 'self' (asked 'could it have been me?': he can't find the player's face anywhere, on the stair or off it). Either way he counts six novices and a seventh with no face, tells of the novices' roll in the warden's niche at the foot of the east stair, and lays the Wrens' brazier.

saltmarrow_aldous_confessed.description: Aldous's Act I confession: '' (untold), 'full' (gentle — the High Keeper put the flame out, a light went down the stair past him, gives the Keeper's sleeve-ember) or 'grudging' (pressed — the bare fact only). Keepers in Act II should know which.

saltmarrow_ferry_lantern_hung.description: Mara hung the green signal lantern on the Saltmarrow dock-post so the Tidewright ferry knows passengers are waiting (Act II bridge).

saltmarrow_pell_ferry_ask.description: What the player told Pell about the ferry: '' (not asked), 'promised' (Pell may come), 'refused' (Pell stays; asks for something lost brought back) or 'undecided' (Pell asks again, loudly, when the ferry comes). Asked on seeing the green lantern or on the dock when the ferry is in.

saltmarrow_mara_saw_sleeve_ember.description: Player showed Mara the Keeper's sleeve-ember Aldous cut from his robe; she warned them Tidewrights don't love Keepers.

saltmarrow_ferry_arrived.description: The Tidewright ferry Slow Mercy sounded its horn and put in at the Saltmarrow dock (region arrival event after the green lantern was hung). Pell moves from Shingle Point to the dock.

saltmarrow_ferry_deed.description: How the player told Oda Farrow their deed (the Tidewright fare): '' (not yet), 'claimed' (I relit the Gull), 'shared' (Saltmarrow did; I carried the ember) or 'brusque' (just take me across). Tidewrights in Act II should know how the Wakebearer talks about their deeds.

saltmarrow_oda_knew_dunstan.description: After the gull burn, Oda Farrow (from off-island) spoke of Dunstan Tollen, who crewed for her; the name would not stay with the Wakebearer. Proof that a burned memory survives off the island (Act II payoff).

saltmarrow_oda_saw_sleeve_ember.description: Player showed Oda Farrow the Keeper's sleeve-ember despite Mara's warning; Tidewrights make Keepers pay twice. Act II Tidewrights may be cooler.

saltmarrow_pell_crossing.description: How Pell's wish to cross ended when the ferry came: '' (unresolved), 'aboard' (Mara gave leave; Pell crosses on the Slow Mercy), 'stayed' (Pell stays and gave the player a finding pouch) or 'let_down' (promised, then the player told Mara Pell should stay). Act II must honour it.

saltmarrow_mara_farewell.description: Mara said goodbye to the player after the ferry's horn (one-time scene).

saltmarrow_mara_message_for_dunstan.description: Mara, knowing Dunstan chose the fog, asked the player to tell him the stool is still there, if they see him. Delivered in person at the end of the long walk (Day 37).

saltmarrow_ferry_passage.description: Oda Farrow gave the player a berth on the Slow Mercy for Thornwold, sailing on the evening tide. Ends Act I (the act-end card); Act II starts from it.

lanes_ferry_at.description: Where the Slow Mercy lies after the crossing: '' (not sailed yet: at the Saltmarrow dock once arrived), 'thornwold' (moored at Thornwold landing), 'saltmarrow' (back at the Saltmarrow dock) 'fen' (at Glasswater Fen's staithe, Day 29) 'wrackholm' (at Wrackholm's jetty, Day 40) 'kindleby' (at Kindleby's quay, Day 62) or 'cindermoor' (at Cindermoor's Boat Stair, down the lane in, Day 81: no lane off that water till the Spire's lit). Oda and the ferry prop are placed by it; the player travels with her.

thornwold_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Thornwold landing (one-time arrival scene after the crossing).

thornwold_pell_landed.description: Pell crossed on the Slow Mercy (saltmarrow_pell_crossing=aboard) and stays at Thornwold's lumber camp, sorting Bram's nails. Moves Pell off the Saltmarrow dock.

thornwold_met_bram.description: Player has met Bram Kettle, foreman of the Tidewright lumber camp at Thornwold landing.

thornwold_bram_knot_grudge.description: Bram Kettle (Saltmarrow-born mother, Tidewright) holds the burning of the founding knot against the player. Tidewright net-makers' resentment of the knot burn (LORE); later Tidewrights may share it.

thornwold_bramble_parted.description: The Wakebearer held the ember to the bramble wall and the canes drew back from it, opening a gap onto the cart road behind. The way into the woods past the wall (through the bramble wall's dialogue).

thornwold_woods_entered.description: Player has seen the arrival scene in the woods past the bramble wall (one-time).

thornwold_met_hob.description: Player has met Hob Marl, the last collier on the near side of the ridge, in the clearing past the bramble wall. He brings the sacks down by the lanterns.

thornwold_hob_stick.description: Player told Hob Marl that Pell found a tally stick by the sacks; it is his ('the night I forgot what I was counting') and he lets Pell keep it. Pell can be told whose it is.

thornwold_hob_paid.description: Player carried Bram's salt crock to Hob Marl: the colliers' first pay since the third load. Bram's tally board gets its fourth salt notch and Hob remembers Bram.

thornwold_ladder_stood.description: The Wakebearer stood the Keepers' fallen ladder back against the last pitch above the stair's landing in the woods. The way up to the ridge (climbing it travels to thornwold_ridge).

thornwold_ridge_reached.description: Player has seen the arrival scene on Thornwold's ridge (one-time, after first climbing the ladder).

thornwold_met_lamp.description: Player has met the Lamp at the lantern bench by the keeper's lodge on the ridge (advances A Light for Thornwold to the_lamp).

thornwold_lamp_coal_told.description: The Lamp showed the player what is in the iron box: the last coal of the Spire's midwinter fire, broken into slivers for the waymark lanterns. When it is spent the lanterns go out.

thornwold_lamp_name_lost.description: The Lamp told the player it had another name once and 'put it somewhere' (forgotten). A Remnant candidate for the Ridge Light's burning.

thornwold_lamp_ladder_told.description: The Lamp admitted putting the ladder down after the fourth collier came up asking for a lantern, so there would be no fifth. The four went on north along the ridge.

thornwold_lamp_heard_of_aldous.description: Player told the Lamp what Brother Aldous confessed in Saltmarrow (reads saltmarrow_aldous_confessed; the Lamp recognises the sleeve-ember's stitching if the player carries it). The coal in the iron box went cold on one side the night of the Snuffing.

thornwold_lamp_heard_seventh.description: Told the Lamp (Wynn) what Aldous counted: six novices with names and a seventh light on the east landing with no face. The Lamp answers Aldous's sorry ('lamp') or weighs the player ('self').

thornwold_stair_light.description: What the player asked of the Lamp for the dark Keepers' stair: '' (not asked), 'sliver' (the Lamp broke a new sliver off the last coal - it shrinks), 'moved' (take the fourth waymark's lantern off the colliers' road - Hob's road gets darker) or 'refused' (the stair stays dark). Shifting paths: the woods' light follows the choice.

thornwold_fourth_lantern_taken.description: The player unhooked the lantern from the fourth waymark on the colliers' road (thornwold_stair_light=moved): that waymark goes dark and its pool of clear ground closes up.

thornwold_stair_lantern_hung.description: The player hung a Keeper's lantern on the bare waymark at the foot of the Keepers' stair (taking down the collier's cap that hung there): the stair stands in clear light.

thornwold_hob_has_cap.description: Player gave Hob Marl the felt cap from the stair's waymark: Ottie Swale's, one of the four colliers who went up after the Lamp. Hob keeps it on the cold hut's seat with the boots. Once Hob gives the boots away (thornwold_boots_away) the cap goes with them.

thornwold_boots_away.description: Hob Marl gave Ottie Swale's boots (and the cap, if he had it) to the player as a Remnant of his memory of the four colliers, for the Ridge Light. The cold hut's seat is bare while it is true; returning the unburned boots sets it false again. Stays true if they are burned.

thornwold_salt_row_away.description: Bram Kettle unpegged the SALT row from his tally board and made it a Remnant of the camp's memory of the colliers, for the Ridge Light. The board's bottom pegs are bare while it is true; returning the unburned stick sets it false again. Stays true if it is burned.

thornwold_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Ridge Light: '' (unlit), 'boots' (Hob Marl's memory of the four colliers who went up after the Lamp — he stops waiting, the cold hut is nobody's) or 'salt_row' (the lumber camp's memory of the colliers and the salt trade — the camp will never know who brings the charcoal). Thornwold's burning; Thornwold forgets it for good.

thornwold_hob_came_in.description: After the Ridge Light was lit, a paid Hob Marl kept his promise and came in to the lumber camp by daylight (one-time arrival scene at the landing). Moves Hob from the clearing to the camp; Bram knows him unless the salt row burned.

thornwold_lamp_saw_light.description: Player has spoken with the Lamp after the Ridge Light was lit (one-time aftermath: the lanterns can go out now; what the coal is kept for).

thornwold_lamp_name.description: The Lamp's name carried home from the Tidewrights' Book (Day 45): '' (not yet), 'told' (the player said it outright: WYNN SALLOW; the Lamp puts its hood back, finishes its sentences, and remembers who told it to keep a coal back the last midwinter) or 'left' (asked first; the Lamp chose to leave it paid in the Book and stay the Lamp, for the four coming down the road).

thornwold_hob_ladder.description: The Fifth (Day 49; salt_row path only — Hob still keeps the four): '' (not yet), 'going' (asked to come up the ladder from the tally-house step, Hob went on ahead; he is off the step), 'up' (the ridge scene seen: the Lamp told him he is the fifth and offered him a lantern; he stands at the ladder's head with it, waiting on the player's word), 'gone' (told to go after the four: he walked north-east up the old Keepers' road with the lantern and hung it on the second bare waymark as he went by, so the next would know he'd gone up) or 'stayed' (told to stay at the bottom of the road: he built a mark by the tally-house step and hung the lantern on it, and cut four notches onto Bram's bare SALT pegs).

thornwold_hob_told_fifth.description: The Fifth: Hob came up the ladder and the Lamp told him he is the fifth, and gave him a lantern lit off the Ridge Light (one-time ridge arrival scene; moves thornwold_hob_ladder from 'going' to 'up').

thornwold_hob_stick_back.description: Pell gave Hob Marl his count-stick back at the tally-house step as he got up to go up the ladder ('Finders keep FOR. You want to know what you were counting now'). On the ridge Hob finishes the half notch.

thornwold_bram_heard_fifth.description: Player told Bram Kettle what became of the old collier on his step after The Fifth (one-time: gone up the ridge, or the mark at the bottom of the road and the notches on the bare SALT pegs).

thornwold_old_road_reached.description: The player has walked out along the old Keepers' road north of the Ridge Light (one-time arrival scene on the spine; only once the Ridge Light is lit).

thornwold_met_ottie.description: Met Ottie Swale at the Northing, the fourth collier who went up after the Lamp, keeping a charcoal fire in the Keepers' fire-basket for the three who went down to the far shore.

thornwold_ottie_cap.description: The player gave Ottie Swale back his felt cap at the Northing (they took it off the stair's waymark and never gave it to Hob). He wears it from then on.

thornwold_northing.description: The Northing (Day 53), what became of the Ridge Light's lantern the Lamp lit for Ottie: '' (not yet), 'lit' (hung on the Northing's boat-lantern hook, a light at the top of the Keepers' steps for the three on the far shore to climb to; Ottie let his charcoal go out and went home to the colliers' clearing and his boots) or 'carried' (put in Ottie's hand: he banked his charcoal with the last sack and took the light down the steps to the three, leaving his boots on his seat).

thornwold_ottie_home_seen.description: Talked with Ottie Swale at home in the colliers' clearing after the Northing was lit (one-time homecoming: his boots, Hob, the three).

thornwold_far_shore_reached.description: The player has gone down the Keepers' steps from the Northing to the far shore (one-time arrival scene; only once there is a light at the Northing or below it: thornwold_northing set).

thornwold_met_wenna_coll.description: Met Wenna Coll at the end of the Keepers' boat-stage on the far shore, waiting for the Spire's boat with the Drays (advances The Far Shore to the_boat).

thornwold_boat_stage_seen.description: Looked at the Keepers' boat-stage on the far shore: the mooring ring worn bright on one side, thirty winters' strokes on the bollard's cap and, after them, Wenna Coll's day-strokes. Wenna knows the player has seen her count.

thornwold_far_shore.description: The Far Shore (Day 55), the Wakebearer's word to Wenna Coll on the boat-stage: '' (not yet), 'up' (somebody came down for them: the three climb the Keepers' steps — with Ottie if he carried the lantern down, and Hob if he went — and walk the old road to the Ridge Light, where the Lamp breaks the warm side of the kept coal into lanterns for their hearths; they come home to the colliers' clearing) or 'waiting' (wait for the boat: the Wakebearer promised to tell the Spire there are colliers on the Northing's stage; they stay on the shore with whatever light they have).

thornwold_ottie_four_home_seen.description: Talked with Ottie Swale at home in the colliers' clearing after the three came up from the far shore (one-time: all four home).

fen_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Glasswater Fen's staithe (one-time arrival scene after the first sailing north-about from Thornwold).

fen_met_hesper.description: Player has met Hesper Vail, Unmoored warden of Stillhithe's staithe.

fen_ember.description: Asked by Hesper to cup the ember on Stillhithe ('it reminds'): 'cupped' (closed their hand over it) or 'bare' (refused). The Unmoored react to it.

fen_heard_of_dunstan.description: Hesper told the player about the big man who rowed to the fen, paid his mooring in whittled gulls, left his name with her and went out along the long walk into the Deeps. Starts The Letting Post.

fen_rowboat_seen.description: Player has looked at the Saltmarrow rowboat tied at Glasswater's staithe (Oda can then name its builder).

fen_dunstan_word.description: What the player left on the Unmoored's letting post for the big man further in: 'mara' (Mara's word: the stool's still by the door), 'own' (someone from Saltmarrow came looking) or 'none' (left nothing: the right to forget). Paid off when Dunstan is found at the end of the long walk (Day 37).

fen_hesper_saw_word.description: Hesper has remarked on what the player left (or didn't) on the letting post (one-time).

fen_met_corran.description: Player has met Corran Teal, the last of the fen folk, at his eel landing.

fen_corran_trap_asked.description: Asked again to be poled out to the Heron, Corran sent the player to lift his far trap at the end of the long walk, in the Deeps' fog, where he won't walk (he doesn't go where the Unmoored go).

fen_corran_decided.description: Corran has decided he likes the player (they lifted his far trap and brought it back; in it, the keeper's skiff bell) and will pole them out to the Heron Light.

fen_punt_out.description: The player is out at the Heron Light's legs in Corran's punt (Corran is there with them, not at his landing). Cleared when he poles them back.

fen_heron_reached.description: Corran has poled the player out through the channels to the Heron Light's legs at least once (the first trip is the full scene).

fen_dunstan_glimpsed.description: At the Heron's legs the player saw a big man with an unlit lantern standing at the edge of the fog on a tussock, looking at the water, before he walked off into it: 'called' (called his name; he stopped, didn't turn, went on), 'watched' (let him go without a word) or 'nameless' (after the gull burn: his name wasn't there to call). Pays off when Dunstan is found.

fen_skiff_bell.description: What the player did with the keeper's skiff bell Corran found in his far trap, at her skiff by the Heron's legs: 'hung' (tied it back on her bow) or 'kept' (kept it). When the Heron is lit the bell rings once by itself, on her bow or in the satchel.

fen_heron_ladder_seen.description: Player has looked at the Heron Light's ladder: the rungs above the slime scraped clean by boots, recently. Someone climbs it (Corran: 'I want a dry day, and you want a reason').

fen_hesper_heard_heron.description: Back from the Heron's legs, the player told Hesper about the trip (her answers follow the bell, the big man and the ladder). She tells them that some nights a small light goes up the Heron's ladder and comes down again: the reason to climb (A Light for Glasswater → up_the_ladder).

fen_heron_climbed.description: The player climbed the Heron's ladder with Corran holding the foot and found the lantern room: the cradle heaped with cold put-down things, a whittled gull on its rim, the keeper's coat folded on the boards. The cradle won't take what nobody holds (→ feed_the_heron).

fen_hesper_name_away.description: Hesper said her name out over the pool until it didn't come back, and gave it to the player as a Remnant (hespers_name) for the Heron. Cleared if the unburned name is given back.

fen_corran_cord_away.description: Corran held his knot-cord out in the fog till it went silver and gave it to the player as a Remnant (corrans_knot_cord): every channel he ever counted back. Cleared if the unburned cord is given back.

fen_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Heron Light: '' (unlit), 'name' (Hesper Vail's name — the last thing she kept; she meets the boats without it) or 'channels' (Corran's knot-cord — nobody living knows the deep channels; the fen folk can't come home through them, and nobody poles out to the Heron again). Glasswater's burning; Glasswater forgets it for good.

fen_lantern_seen.description: Back on the fen after Glasswater's burning, the player saw the lantern lit at the fog's foot set down at the end of the long walk (one-time arrival scene; starts For After).

fen_dunstan_met.description: The player found Dunstan Tollen at the end of the long walk, sat on a tussock by his lit lantern, whittling, and he said his name (after the gull burn it slides off). Completes For After.

fen_dunstan_mara.description: What the player told Dunstan of Mara: 'message' (her word, in person or tied on the post — he whittled a gull for the stool, facing the door), 'burned' (that she says Tollens end with her and sets out two cups — the gull burn), 'spared' (after the gull burn, only that she's well), 'well' (that she's well) or 'nothing' (not theirs to carry).

fen_dunstan_rule.description: Whether the player asked Dunstan what he came to put down ('asked' — he doesn't know: 'that's how you know it went') or kept Stillhithe's rule ('kept').

fen_hesper_heard_dunstan.description: Hesper has been told the big man was found by his lit lantern (one-time): she keeps his name till he comes for it.

fen_oda_heard_heron.description: Oda has been told about the trip out to the Heron's legs (the bell, the big man) — one-time.

fen_oda_heard_dunstan.description: Oda has been told Dunstan was found (one-time): 'Is he laughing?'

saltmarrow_mara_got_gull.description: The player gave Mara the gull Dunstan whittled for her at the end of the long walk; she set it on his stool facing the door.

fen_oda_lane_asked.description: Oda told the player where the lane runs on from the lit fen: east-about to Wrackholm. Once Dunstan is found (the player 'done here') she'll sail it.

wrackholm_landed.description: First landfall at Wrackholm played (the arrival scene: the yard dark, the answering horn lashed). Starts A Light for Wrackholm.

wrackholm_met_wenna.description: The player met Wenna Garrow, lane-warden of Wrackholm, by the lashed horn and heard why nobody answers (a horn answered is a lane promised) and of the Gannet.

wrackholm_met_jory.description: The player met Jory Pask stripping the Gannet's copper in the yard.

wrackholm_board_read.description: The player held the ember to the Gannet's blank crew board and the chalk came back: Hale Corbet, master; Annis Corbet; Ruan Pask.

wrackholm_gannet_named.description: Wenna said the Gannet's crew's names into the lashed horn (The Gannet's Crew done), and told the player it was her answer brought them in.

wrackholm_jory_brother.description: The player told Jory his brother's name, off the crew board: Ruan Pask.

wrackholm_who_answered.description: What the player told Jory about who called the Gannet in: '' (not asked), 'wenna' (the truth: Wenna answered, and the Wrack went out), 'keepers' (the Spire was put out on purpose, by Keepers) or 'dark' (nobody's to blame for the dark). For Wrackholm's burning and the Tidewrights' arc.

wrackholm_wenna_saw_sleeve.description: The player showed Wenna the Keeper's sleeve-ember: Keepers pay twice, once for the crossing and once into the lane-house Book (their names).

wrackholm_book_told.description: Wenna told the player the Lamp's name may be in the lane-house Book of Keepers carried (if it ever rode a Tidewright deck); she'll find its page once the Wrack is lit.

wrackholm_wenna_offer.description: Wenna weighed the player's deeds (three lit) and offered to swear them a friend of the lanes once the Wrack is lit: the Tidewrights court the Wakebearer.

wrackholm_jory_float.description: Jory gave the player a glass float off the come-home pile for Pell's finding pouch (something lost, something good).

saltmarrow_pell_float.description: The player brought Pell the glass float from Wrackholm in the finding pouch: something lost, something GOOD. It sits on top of the lost-things crate.

wrackholm_teeth_marks_told.description: Wenna remembered that nobody ever knew the way across the Teeth by heart: you put your feet on the white, the lampwardens' white-lead marks, renewed every spring (the fog will have had them off). She sent the player to wait the spring tide down at the spit's end.

wrackholm_tide.description: The tide off Wrackholm's spit: '' (in: the Teeth under, the usual state) or 'low' (the bottom of the springs: the Teeth stand up out of the water enough to walk). Waited down at the spit's end; the flood comes back behind the player as they cross back from the Teeth. A local story value until day/night and tides exist as a system.

wrackholm_teeth_marks.description: At low water the player held the ember to the first rock off the spit and the lampwardens' white-lead marks came back, rock after rock out into the fog toward the Wrack: the way across the Teeth.

wrackholm_teeth_crossed.description: The player crossed the Teeth on the white for the first time (the crossing scene on reaching them).

wrackholm_jory_up.description: With the Gannet's copper off, Jory went up the shingle to Wenna, as he said he would once he knew it was her answer (who answered = wenna); he stands by her at the horn after.

wrackholm_board_leave.description: With the Wrack wanting feeding, Wenna (the yard) gave leave for the Gannet's crew board to be prised off her transom for it: a year and a tide, and nobody is coming for her now.

wrackholm_board_taken.description: The Gannet's crew board is off her transom (the player prised it off with Wenna's leave; it's in the satchel, or burned). Set back to false if the player puts it back unburned.

wrackholm_beacon_burned.description: What fed the Wrack Light (Wrackholm's burning): '' (not lit), 'answer' (Wenna's answer: nobody on Wrackholm remembers she ever answered a horn, the Gannet's night included), 'board' (the Gannet's crew board: the crew unnamed again on Wrackholm, for good) or 'white' (Hale's white-lead pot: Jory's one day out on the Teeth behind Ruan; nobody left on the island has walked behind a lampwarden).

wrackholm_horn_sounded.description: With the Wrack lit, Wenna cut the lashing off the answering horn and it was sounded (it takes two: Jory, if he came up, else the player); Oda's horn answered from the jetty if the ferry lay there.

wrackholm_book_opened.description: Wenna opened the lane-house Book for the player by lamplight. Its last line, the night of the Snuffing, is a name the fog has had, in a hand that wrote fast; nobody on Wrackholm wrote it or saw it written. The ember leaned to it and the player shut the Book without deciding to (mystery #2 hook; never explain yet).

wrackholm_lamp_name_read.description: In the lane-house Book, thirty winters back, the player read the Lamp's name in its own hand: WYNN SALLOW, keeper, for the Ridge Light. Paid twice. (To carry back to the Lamp.)

wrackholm_sworn.description: Wenna's offer, at the scale over the lane-house door once the Wrack was lit and the horn sounded: '' (not answered), 'sworn' (sworn a friend of the lanes: no Tidewright deck will weigh the player light) or 'declined'. For the Tidewrights' and Keepers' arcs.

lanes_oda_weighed_name.description: Oda has weighed the Lamp's name being carried home off the Book (one-time line at Thornwold landing once thornwold_lamp_name is set; differs for a friend of the lanes).

fen_dunstan_walk.description: Dunstan's walk back for his name (Day 51, The Walk Back): '' (still at the end of the long walk, nearly done), 'coming' (after the Wrack was lit, back on the fen: his lantern has come halfway in along the long walk and stopped — the boards are laid for going in), 'in' (walked in behind the player's ember; at the staithe's foot to ask Hesper for it himself), 'home' (named; rowed his boat home to Saltmarrow facing backward, and sits on his stool by Mara's door) or 'stayed' (named; stays on the fen and lays the long walk's boards the other way, for whoever walks back next — the first of the Unmoored to mend anything).

saltmarrow_mara_saw_dunstan_home.description: Mara has spoken of Dunstan coming home, rowing in backward (one-time; after the gull burn she doesn't know him, and the second cup is his anyway).

thornwold_bend.description: The Bend in the Road (Day 57), Wenna Coll's walk out along the old cart road to the hearth she lost the night the road started lying: '' (not asked), 'asked' (the player said they'd walk out with her at first light), 'morning' (the next arrival in the woods: she waits by the first waymark past the wall, lantern held over the ruts), 'walked' (out along the old bend with her to her hearth, Coll's Hearth: her clamp burned right through untended), then where the Lamp's coal went — 'road' (hung on the bend's Keepers' waymark: the bend is a road again, anybody can find her and her charcoal comes down the cart road to the gap) or 'hearth' (kept on a stake by her own hut door: a light of her own, as she wanted; the road still lies about her and her sacks go down with Hob's cart).

thornwold_bend_first_light.description: The morning after Wenna Coll was asked (The Bend in the Road): the next arrival in the woods played the first-light scene (one-time).

thornwold_bend_breaking_out.description: Coll's Hearth after The Bend in the Road (Day 58): the next arrival found Wenna at her clamp with the rake, breaking it out a sack at a time (one-time arrival scene; from then on she stands at the clamp's open front instead of sitting by her door).

thornwold_colls_hearth_reached.description: The player has walked the old bend with Wenna Coll to Coll's Hearth (one-time arrival scene).

thornwold_wenna_clamp_seen.description: The player looked at Wenna Coll's spent clamp at Coll's Hearth (Wenna has a word for it after).

saltmarrow_aldous_heard_walk_back.description: Aldous has been told Dunstan walked back out of the fog (home, or staying on the fen to turn the boards) — one-time: nine hundred years the Keepers said the fog gives nothing back; 'a lie, or only true while the Spire burned'.

wrackholm_oda_lane_asked.description: At Wrackholm with the Wrack lit, Oda told the player where the lane runs on: south-about down the Taper to Kindleby, the Keepers' mother-house (Day 62). Opens the Taper on the lane map.

kindleby_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Kindleby (one-time arrival scene: the candles, the bell that answered before Oda blew, Brother Tobin at the quay).

kindleby_met_provost.description: The player has met Agathe Lorn, Provost of Kindleby, at the chapter-house door (her first words are said once).

kindleby_rite.description: What the player told the Provost about the rite (Day 62): '' (not answered, or 'I'll think on it'), 'bowed' (bow to the rite: the chapter sits and chooses what Kindleby can spare, and the Wakebearer carries its choice up the stair) or 'refused' (the Wakebearer chooses, as on every other island). For Kindleby's burning and the Keepers' arc.

kindleby_provost_heard_aldous.description: The player told the Provost what Aldous said: the High Keeper put the flame out (Day 62). She holds to the order's word, 'the Firstflame failed' — and, if the confession was full, a light went down the stair past him: '...Did he.'

kindleby_provost_heard_lamp.description: The player told the Provost of the Lamp on Thornwold (Day 62): named (thornwold_lamp_name=told: Wynn Sallow, written dead in the Long Book, is struck through, not scraped) or not (left: 'That's not a name, that's a post').

kindleby_told_of_stage.description: The Wakebearer kept the far shore's promise (thornwold_far_shore=waiting): they told the Provost there are colliers waiting on the Northing's boat-stage for the Spire's boat. 'There is no Spire to tell. There's me. Very well: you've told the Spire.' She will put it to the chapter that the skiff goes north.

kindleby_ring_held.description: The Wakebearer held Kindleby's ring from the crown while the chapter sat (Day 64): every brother and sister off the candles for an hour, the candles let gutter, the fog held off by the ember alone. The chapter chose the boats' night, and an old brother, Anselm, carried the Boats' Lantern out into the fog to make it a Remnant. For the Keepers' arc: Keepers met later can know the Wakebearer held Kindleby's door.

kindleby_skiff_north.description: While the chapter sat, two sisters ran the chapter's skiff down the shingle and rowed north with oil, meal and a lantern for the colliers waiting on the Northing's stage (only if kindleby_told_of_stage; Day 64). The skiff is gone from Kindleby's quay until it lands on the far shore and rows back (thornwold_skiff, Day 66).

kindleby_beacon_burned.description: What fed the Vigil Light (Kindleby's burning, Day 64): '' (not lit), 'boats' (the chapter's choice, the Boats' Lantern: Kindleby's night of the boats is gone — the lanterns on the quay, the faces up the steps, what the ones who came over from the Spire saw and never said; nobody on Kindleby remembers how they came) or 'pan' (Tobin's coal-pan: Tobin Ashe was never called up and will never think to go). Read with kindleby_rite: bowed and pan is the rite kept and broken the same night.

thornwold_skiff_landed.description: The player has seen Kindleby's skiff in at the Northing's boat-stage (one-time arrival scene on the far shore once kindleby_skiff_north: Sister Hild Garrow and Sister Pim with oil, meal and a lantern; Day 66).

thornwold_skiff.description: What came of Kindleby's skiff on the far shore (Day 66): '' (not landed, or landed and waiting on the Wakebearer's word), 'home' (Wenna Coll took the meal and went home up the Keepers' steps: thornwold_far_shore becomes 'up' and the homecoming follows), 'kindleby' (whoever was on the shore got into the skiff: Wenna and the Drays — Ottie if he carried the lantern down, Hob if he went — keep candles on Kindleby now) or 'empty' (the colliers had already gone up before it landed; the sisters left the meal on the stage and rowed back). The skiff is back on Kindleby's shingle once it is set.

saltmarrow_aldous_boat.description: Aldous's answer to the Provost's offer of a boat (kindleby_provost_heard_aldous; Day 66): '' (not told yet), 'letter' (he won't get in a boat to be weighed by a chapter, but he wrote it down: the player carries Aldous's Letter to Kindleby) or 'no' (he won't go and won't write: 'Tell her I'm sorry about the reports').

kindleby_provost_read_letter.description: The Provost read Aldous Wren's letter (Day 66): she puts him on the page at the back of the Long Book for what was seen — empty a long while. For the Keepers' arc and Act III (the chapter has a Keeper's written word that the High Keeper put the flame out).

kindleby_stair_taper.description: The ember gave something back (Day 69, What the Ember Keeps): as the Vigil Light caught, its smoke closed round the Wakebearer's hand and left the Stair-Taper in it — the Wakebearer's first own Remnant (item kind 'own'), a novice's notched taper for the Spire's east stair. Given in the Vigil Light's kindling, or at the lit door for saves from before Day 69.

kindleby_provost_saw_taper.description: The Provost of Kindleby saw the Stair-Taper (Day 69): a novice's light for the east stair; she'd not remember a novice — they all had the same face under the hood. 'Keep it out of the chapter's sight. They'd want to weigh it.' For the Keepers' arc: a Keeper who has seen the Wakebearer carry a novice's taper.

kindleby_tobin_saw_taper.description: Brother Tobin saw the Stair-Taper (Day 69): he knows it from the letter in his coal-pan — unless the pan fed the Vigil Light (kindleby_beacon_burned=pan), when he feels he ought to know it and doesn't.

kindleby_oda_low_water_asked.description: Oda told of the Low Water (Day 72, Act II's close step 2; asked at Kindleby's quay once the Vigil Light is lit): shallow water south of the ring between Kindleby and the Gull, skerries and a Keepers' light on Lowsong rock, where the fog is heard singing ('the Hollow Choir', pilots' talk). Tidewrights go round it; the Slow Mercy won't sail it. The chart shows it from then on (a landmark, not a port). Starts The Low Water.

kindleby_hild_low_water.description: Sister Hild will row the Wakebearer out to the Low Water in the chapter's skiff once its bottom is scraped clean (Day 72); she rows them once the Provost gives leave (Day 75).

saltmarrow_aldous_saw_taper.description: Brother Aldous saw the Stair-Taper (Day 69): one of his, cut in the warden's niche at the foot of the east stair, a notch to a landing. If he confessed in full, he tells that the light that went down the stair past him the night of the Snuffing went down counting landings.

kindleby_provost_low_water.description: The Provost gave leave for Hild to row the Wakebearer out to the Low Water (Day 75): nobody goes out in the wet, and then yes — it's a Keepers' light, and it's the Wakebearer asking. She wrote Lowsong's Keeper, Brother Iver Lusk, in the Long Book with the drowned.

lowsong_out.description: Kindleby's skiff is out at Lowsong with Hild and the Wakebearer (Day 75): set as Hild rows out, cleared as she rows back. Hild and the skiff are on Lowsong's landing while it holds, and off Kindleby's shingle.

lowsong_landed.description: The Wakebearer has been rowed out to Lowsong once (Day 75, the arrival event lowsong_rowing_out: past Kindleby's candles into the singing).

lowsong_met_keeper.description: The Wakebearer met Brother Iver Lusk, Keeper of Lowsong, alive on his rock with one small lamp lit and the light cold (Day 75). Completes The Low Water and opens A Light for Lowsong.

lowsong_keeper_saw_taper.description: Brother Iver saw the Stair-Taper (Day 75): a stair-taper, burned past the third notch — and the nearest voice in the Choir went quiet while it was out. (Mystery #2/#4 foreshadow; future.)

lowsong_iver_gave.description: What Brother Iver put down into a Remnant for Lowsong's light, with the ember beside him (Day 77, A Light for Lowsong): '' (nothing, or it was given back), 'lamp' (Iver's Lamp: his three months' listening and the nearest voice in the Choir) or 'key' (Iver's Cell Key: Kindleby, the chapter, the way home). The fog on the Low Water leaves nothing lying, so Lowsong's Remnant is made on purpose.

lowsong_beacon_burned.description: What fed Lowsong's light (Lowsong's burning, Day 77): '' (not lit), 'lamp' (Iver's Lamp: he never heard a voice in the singing — it's wind in the skerries to him — and he rows home to Kindleby with Hild) or 'key' (Iver's Cell Key: he doesn't know there was anywhere else, and keeps the light, and listens, and is glad of it). The Choir goes further off once the light is lit either way.

lowsong_iver_home.description: Brother Iver rowed home to Kindleby with Hild and the Wakebearer after his lamp fed Lowsong's light (Day 77). He keeps candles by the chapter-house now; the Provost struck him out of the Long Book's drowned.

lowsong_hood_pin.description: The ember gave something back as Lowsong's light caught (Day 77): the Hood-Pin, the Wakebearer's second own Remnant (item kind 'own') — a novice's bone hood-pin, and the east stair again: the wind off the lantern room, a hand pinning the hood forward ('Nobody's to see your face on this stair tonight'), and the landings being counted aloud until the hand says hush.

lowsong_keeper_saw_pin.description: Brother Iver saw the Hood-Pin (Day 77): a novice's pin, given out at the foot of the stair with the tapers. If he still listens (lowsong_beacon_burned=key) the nearest voice stops again while it's out; if not, he thinks something stopped, and decides it's the wind. (Mystery #2/#4; future.)

kindleby_provost_heard_iver.description: The Provost heard what became of Brother Iver after Lowsong's light was lit (Day 77): home (she struck him out of the Long Book's drowned, her first line ever struck) or staying on the rock not knowing Kindleby (she writes him in again, under the light).

greying_turned_back.description: The Greying has turned the Wakebearer back at least once (the ember ran out: "You forget why you came."). Set by GreyingWalker, saved; NPCs may remark on it (Aldous, Day 78).

saltmarrow_aldous_heard_turned_back.description: Player told Aldous the fog turned them back; he told of the ember's ring of clear and Isolde's ember walking her out (Day 78).

kindleby_oda_lane_in.description: Oda saw Lowsong's light from the Slow Mercy's rail and counted six lights, 'the lights between' (Day 79, Act II's end): she inked the lane in on her chart, from Kindleby's quay to Cindermoor, the way the Keepers' boats came out the week of the Snuffing. Never a Tidewright lane. The chart shows it from then on; Oda will take the Wakebearer in when asked.

cindermoor_passage.description: Oda agreed to take the Wakebearer in to Cindermoor on the morning ebb, down the lane in from Kindleby (Day 79): Act II ends here (the act2 end card). The crossing in itself opens Act III, The Spire.

cindermoor_crossed.description: The Slow Mercy went down the lane in from Kindleby on the morning ebb (Day 81, Act III opens): Tobin's one stroke on the quay bell, Oda steering by the six lights astern, Cindermoor out of the fog. Sets lanes_ferry_at to 'cindermoor'.

cindermoor_landed.description: The first landing at Cindermoor's Boat Stair has played (the arrival scene: the quay, the fog, Merrit on the bollard; starts The Way Up).

cindermoor_oda_waiting.description: Oda has told the Wakebearer she'll wait at the Boat Stair (no lane off that water till the Spire's lit).

cindermoor_merrit_met.description: The Wakebearer has spoken with Brother Merrit Coyle, the Hushed boat-warden on the Boat Stair: 'Eight slips. Seven out. One in.'

cindermoor_merrit_asked_aboard.description: The Wakebearer asked Merrit to come aboard the Mercy; he won't leave the stair ('Then who'd be on the stair?'). Oda puts a cup by him of an evening.

cindermoor_merrit_saw_pin.description: Merrit saw the Hood-Pin and stopped humming for one line: 'Pin's straight. Good. Nobody's to see.' (Mystery #2 foreshadow.)

cindermoor_merrit_saw_taper.description: Merrit counted the Stair-Taper's notches: 'Past the third. You went higher than you were told.' (Mystery #2 foreshadow.)

cindermoor_saw_slips.description: The Wakebearer looked at the boathouse on the Boat Stair: eight slips, seven empty, and in the eighth a Keepers' boat never launched. Whose it was is Act III's.

cindermoor_oda_on_merrit.description: Oda on Merrit calling her novice, and on leaving him be.

cindermoor_oda_on_slips.description: Oda on the eighth slip: she counted seven boats past the Taper and never thought to count what didn't come.

cindermoor_road_tried.description: The Wakebearer followed the cinder road into the fog and found it had forgotten where it goes (The Way Up → the_cressets).

cindermoor_cresset_stair_1.description: The first waymark cresset at the turn of the cinder road above the Boat Stair, lit from the ember (Day 82): the road remembers as far as the second, up the notch.

cindermoor_cresset_stair_2.description: The second cresset, at the top of the notch where the road forgot, lit (Day 82): the road remembers over the lip onto the long steps (the exit opens).

cindermoor_cresset_steps_1.description: Long steps cresset 1 lit from the ember (Day 82), at the lip: the first leg west along the lowest step and up the first turn.

cindermoor_cresset_steps_2.description: Long steps cresset 2 lit from the ember (Day 82), at the first turn: the second leg east and up.

cindermoor_cresset_steps_3.description: Long steps cresset 3 lit from the ember (Day 82), at the second turn: the third leg west and up.

cindermoor_cresset_steps_4.description: Long steps cresset 4 lit from the ember (Day 82), at the third turn, on the shoulder: the last leg east as far as the Unmoored sitting at its edge.

cindermoor_steps_reached.description: Came up over the lip of the notch onto Cindermoor's long steps (Day 82; the arrival scene).

cindermoor_ness_met.description: Met Ness Garrow, one of the Unmoored who came to Cindermoor on purpose because the fog is thickest there, at the edge of the fourth cresset's light (Day 82).

cindermoor_ness_ember.description: What the Wakebearer did when Ness asked them to cover the ember at the edge of the light (Day 82): 'cupped' (closed their hand over it) or 'bare' (let it burn). The Unmoored on the long steps turn from a bare ember.

cindermoor_doused_seen.description: Looked at the cresset past the Unmoored on the long steps: put out on purpose, raked and packed with wet cinder (Day 82). The way on up waits on it.

cindermoor_cresset_steps_5.description: The doused cresset past the Unmoored on the long steps relit (Day 83: dug out from the ember by the Wakebearer over Ness's wish; Day 85: or by Sister Hild for the chapter, cindermoor_keepers_relit): the road remembers up to the crown, and the Unmoored go off along the shoulder into the fog.

cindermoor_way_on.description: How the Wakebearer first went on up past the doused cresset to the crown (Day 83): 'relit' (dug it out and lit it, over the Unmoored's wish) or 'led' (Ness walked them up in the dark by the rake, the ember covered). Relighting it after being led sets 'relit'.

cindermoor_crown_reached.description: Came up onto Cindermoor's crown, to the Hearthspire's foot (Day 83; the arrival scene, The Way Up done).

cindermoor_niche_seen.description: Looked into the warden's niche beside the east stair door at the Spire's foot (Day 83): Aldous's seat, his tapers and his knife on the shelf.

cindermoor_roll_read.description: Read the novices' roll in the warden's niche (Day 83): seven names for the last midwinter in the door-warden's hand, and the seventh scraped out with a blade, not struck through. Starts The Seventh Name.

cindermoor_roll_boats.description: Turned the novices' roll over in the warden's niche (Day 83): the boat-warden's list for the night of the Snuffing on the back, seven boats and their crews, and the eighth 'kept back. Her word.' The eighth slip's first clue.

cindermoor_stair_door_tried.description: Tried the east stair door at the Spire's foot (Day 83): ajar on the dark, the wind coming down; the Wakebearer stops on the threshold counting and can't think what comes after one. The east stair waits (Act III step 8).

cindermoor_ring_seen.description: Noticed the path worn round the Hearthspire's foot in the cinder (Day 83): one person's, walked round and round, the woman 'higher up' who doesn't sit (never named yet).

cindermoor_merrit_seven_lit.description: Back at the Boat Stair after relighting the doused cresset, Merrit counted seven lights up the moor (Day 83): 'Seven out. Seven lit. Somebody's coming down, then.'

cindermoor_chapter_came.description: The chapter's boat came in to the Boat Stair (Day 85, Act III step 4): back down off the moor once the crown was reached, the Wakebearer finds the first of the seven Spire boats coming in under oars from Kindleby with the Provost, Sister Hild at the steering oar, Brother Iver if he rowed home, and Wenna Coll with a box of candles if the colliers went to keep candles on Kindleby. Merrit holds the bow. Starts The Chapter.

cindermoor_chapter_claim.description: What the Wakebearer said when the Provost laid the chapter's claim on them at the Boat Stair (Day 85): the chapter will go up to the Spire's foot and sit, and choose what the Hearthspire is given, and the Wakebearer carries its choice up the east stair — 'the hand, not the choosing'. '' (not yet told), 'heard' (the chapter can sit; I'll hear what it says) or 'refused' (I've chosen six times; I'll choose the seventh). For the chapter's sitting and the lantern room.

cindermoor_chapter_weigh.description: Whether the Wakebearer let the Provost hold the Stair-Taper and the Hood-Pin at the Boat Stair to weigh them (Day 85): '' (not asked), 'shown' (she held them — cold, a candle-end and a bit of bone, to her — and gave them back: 'Weighing isn't taking. Not yet.') or 'kept' (no: 'Then it'll weigh you instead'). For the chapter's sitting and the east stair (mystery #1/#2).

cindermoor_provost_heard_roll.description: The Wakebearer told the Provost of the novices' roll at the Boat Stair (Day 85): a seventh name scraped, not struck through. A Keeper's hand won't scrape a name; the door-warden kept the roll; 'I'll want to see it.' (The Seventh Name → a_keeper_knows.)

cindermoor_chapter_road.description: The Provost asked about the road up at the Boat Stair (Day 85): seven lit by the Wakebearer already, or — if Ness led them up in the dark — Hild goes up with the bow lantern and relights the doused cresset (cindermoor_keepers_relit).

cindermoor_keepers_relit.description: The Keepers relit the doused cresset (Day 85): the Wakebearer was led up in the dark by Ness and left it doused, and the chapter came in; Hild dug it out in ten minutes with the bow lantern. The Unmoored went off along the shoulder into the fog, Ness with her rake this time. Sets cindermoor_cresset_steps_5 too.

cindermoor_asked_spare.description: The Wakebearer asked the Provost to leave the doused cresset out for the Unmoored (Day 85): 'A Keeper doesn't leave a light out because somebody in the dark asked her to.' She relit it anyway, and wrote down that they asked.

cindermoor_chapter_up.description: The Provost said when (Day 86): at dusk, once the claim was laid and the road asked after, the chapter went up the lit road from the Boat Stair to sit at the Spire's foot (the chapter's NPCs move from the quay to the crown; Cindermoor's light goes to dusk). The Chapter → the_sitting.

cindermoor_chapter_sat.description: The chapter sat at the Spire's foot (Day 86, region event on reaching the crown after cindermoor_chapter_up): the Long Book has every island's burning for nine hundred years and not one line for what the Hearthspire burned; Hild lifts the warden's seat in the niche and a stair goes down into the Spire's lower rooms, where the Spire kept its own book. The chapter will read before it chooses — tomorrow. Night on Cindermoor. The Chapter → the_lower_rooms.

cindermoor_sitting_spoke.description: What the Wakebearer said at the chapter's sitting (Day 86) when the Long Book was found to have no line for the Spire: '' (not yet), 'offered' (weigh the ember, then: 'Not till we know what it's fed on'), 'asked' (the Spire kept its own book: the Provost remembers Aldous saying he sat on the oldest thing in the order) or 'silent' (the hand doesn't speak at a sitting: 'Thank you.'). For the lower rooms and the lantern room.

cindermoor_morning.description: The night after the sitting passed (Day 87): the Wakebearer lay down by the chapter's candles at the Spire's foot till morning (the foot_rest object). Morning on Cindermoor (light and fog overrides ahead of the night ones); the chapter goes down the stair under the warden's seat to the lower rooms (its NPCs leave the crown).

cindermoor_spire_book_read.description: The chapter read the Spire's own book in the lower rooms (Day 87, Act III step 5, region event): nine hundred midwinters of the Hushed 'given' to the flame 'and what was in them'; the Hushed are filled, not emptied, with what the islands burned; if the flame is not fed, all it was given comes home (the Greying). The last page is the High Keeper's, Oriel Sayre, named: 'It is starved, and I am starving it.' The Chapter → the_spire_book.

cindermoor_spire_line.description: Who wrote the Spire's line into the Long Book in the lower rooms (Day 87): '' (not yet), 'provost' (the Provost, in her own hand, and under it 'I never asked'), 'hand' (the Wakebearer, whose hand makes a Keeper's letters without knowing it would — mystery #2) or 'open' (nobody: the Spire's line left unwritten, which has never been done either). For the lantern room.

cindermoor_eighth_sought.description: After the Spire's own book (Day 89): the Provost reckons the High Keeper never left the island (the eighth boat still on its rollers, one pair of feet round the Spire) and the chapter comes back up from the lower rooms to the crown with the Wakebearer to look. Moves the chapter's NPCs up; the woman walks the ring path.

cindermoor_eighth_seen.description: The crown arrival after cindermoor_eighth_sought (Day 89): the woman on the ring path seen walking round the Spire's foot by daylight; the Provost says 'Oriel' and she doesn't turn.

cindermoor_eighth_met.description: The Wakebearer stepped onto the ring path and the woman stopped for them (Day 89).

cindermoor_eighth_told.description: What the Wakebearer did with what the Spire's book says about the woman on the ring path (Day 89): '' (not yet), 'told' (her name, Oriel Sayre, and what she did and why: she takes it on their word, sits down, and stops walking), 'asked' (whether she wants it back: 'Not yet' — ask again after the east stair) or 'kept' (said nothing and let her walk: 'Kind. Or careful.'). For the east stair and the lantern room.

cindermoor_choir_heard.description: At the east stair door after the Wakebearer answered the woman on the ring path (Day 90, Act III step 7): singing comes down the stair (the Hollow Choir, at the Spire), and the nearest voice gets two words out: 'Not Hushed.' Starts The Nearest Voice; the Choir is heard on the crown from here on.

cindermoor_choir_down.description: The Wakebearer told the Provost what the nearest voice said (Day 90): every line in the Spire's book says Hushed, so she takes them back down to the lower rooms to read the middle of it.

cindermoor_choir_line_read.description: The lower rooms' arrival after cindermoor_choir_down (Day 90): the Provost reads the Spire's book through and finds the one line in nine hundred that says Not Hushed — a Wakebearer who came up the east stair asking, given to the flame awake, her name scraped off it and kept on the story: Isolde Vane.

cindermoor_choir_answered.description: What the Wakebearer did at the east stair door with Isolde Vane's name (Day 90): '' (not yet), 'named' (said it up the stair: the nearest voice says 'Yes' and stops singing), 'written' (the Provost wrote her in the Long Book as she was, Not Hushed, and struck the old story through) or 'left' (let her sing: it's hers to get out). For the east stair and the lantern room.

cindermoor_stair_climbed.description: The Wakebearer went up the east stair (Day 92, The Last Landing): the Stair-Taper lit from the ember for the stair it was cut for, the count going past one, the Provost counting the hand up from the foot. Seven landings to the last, under the lantern room.

cindermoor_isolde_spoke.description: Going up the east stair past Isolde Vane when she'd been left to sing (cindermoor_choir_answered=left, Day 92): she got the rest out — 'Not Hushed. Awake. I asked them.' — and, to the Wakebearer going by, 'Somebody went down this way not long ago. Counting. With a coal.'

cindermoor_stair_remembered.description: On the last landing (Day 92, mystery #2 paid): the count finished and the Wakebearer remembered — a Kindleby novice, the seventh on the roll, who went up past the third landing the night of the Snuffing, found the High Keeper with the last coal, asked to carry it, and fed it everything they were on the way down; Oriel pinned their hood and scraped their name. Their name came back (never said aloud or shown). The ember is made of them.

cindermoor_stair_down.description: The Wakebearer came back down the east stair from the last landing (Day 92): the Provost counted the hand down at the door ('That's the second stroke') and saw their face with the hood back; then the novices' roll (cindermoor_seventh_answered).

cindermoor_provost_knows.description: Coming down the east stair (Day 92) the Wakebearer told the Provost it was them: the coal kept back, 'in hands that asked to carry it' — a Kindleby novice, one of hers, whose face she doesn't remember. If unset she saw the face and wasn't told.

cindermoor_seventh_answered.description: What the Wakebearer did with the seventh place on the novices' roll after the last landing (Day 92, The Seventh Name done): '' (not yet), 'written' (their own name written back in, upright Keeper's letters), 'struck' (written and struck through: the novice is finished) or 'left' (left scraped, as Oriel left it, so nobody could write them down for the giving). For the lantern room.

cindermoor_oriel_knows.description: Told Oriel Sayre the Wakebearer was the novice she gave the last coal to on the last landing (Day 93, What She Was to You). An asked Oriel takes her name then too; a kept one asks who she gave it to first, then her name. Her ring-path name gives way to 'Oriel Sayre'.

cindermoor_oriel_choice.description: What the Wakebearer asked of Oriel once she knew them (Day 93): '' (not yet), 'climb' (come up to the lantern room: she waits at the east stair door, 'carry nothing and touch nothing'), 'boat' (her boat's in the eighth slip: she goes down to the Boat Stair to sit in it and see the Spire from the water; Hild greases the rollers) or 'own' (not choosing for her: she stands at the foot with the chapter, a pace behind the Provost). For the lantern room.

cindermoor_chapter_chose.description: The chapter's last sitting at the Spire's foot, by daylight (Day 95, Act III step 9): once Oriel's been asked (`cindermoor_oriel_choice`), the Provost sits the chapter on the one line — whether the Hearthspire is lit again — and writes that it does not choose: 'The hand that carried it down carries it up.' Opens the stair on up from the last landing to the lantern room.

cindermoor_provost_would_light.description: At the last sitting (Day 95) the Wakebearer asked the Provost what she'd choose: she'd light it, tonight, 'and I'd be wrong in some way I can't see from here' — which is why it isn't hers. For the ending.

cindermoor_lantern_room_entered.description: Up the last of the east stair into the Hearthspire's lantern room (Day 95, Act III step 9, mystery #4's close): the cold cradle, the soot-black panes, and the Hollow Choir — everything the Firstflame ate that had nobody left to go home to, kept together by singing since Isolde Vane woke among them.

cindermoor_cradle_held.description: The Wakebearer held the ember out over the lantern room's cradle (Day 95): it would take, the room stopped singing to listen, and they took their hand back — not till they know what they'd be asking. The final choice (step 9's close) reads it.

cindermoor_ring_weighed.description: At the lantern room's cradle once the ember's been held over it (Day 96), the Wakebearer thought of the six lights and what each one cost (a line per burning) — once.

cindermoor_cradle_choice.description: The final choice at the lantern room's cradle (Day 96, Act III step 9's close): '' (not yet), 'lit' (the ember put in the ash: the Hearthspire burns, the grey goes back, and it took the Wakebearer's own past first — the Stair-Taper and Hood-Pin burn; by midwinter it will be hungry), 'released' (the ember let go out of the open casement: it walked the Hollow Choir out to the six lights and spent itself; the Spire stays dark and the Wakebearer's hand holds a cold coal) or 'dark' (the hand closed on it: the Spire stays dark, the Choir sings on, the ring of six holds and each island chooses its own midwinter burning; the ember goes round the ring).

cindermoor_counted_down.description: Back down the east stair after the cradle (Day 96): the Provost counted the Wakebearer down, wrote the Long Book's last line under the chapter's (as the cradle was chosen), and a witness signed it; the Long Book shut. Ends Act III (the act3 card).

cindermoor_oda_after_seen.description: Oda has told the Wakebearer, at the Boat Stair after the count down, what the night looked like from the Mercy (Day 97, per ending).

cindermoor_lane_out.description: The epilogue (Day 97): Oda has sailed the Wakebearer off Cindermoor's water to Kindleby after the ending — by the lit Spire's light astern (lit), by the six lights warm ahead (released), or by the ember held up in the bow (dark). From then the lane runs both ways (Oda's 'Take me back in to Cindermoor.').

kindleby_homecoming_seen.description: The epilogue on Kindleby (Day 97, arrival event kindleby_homecoming): Tobin rings the quay bell's second stroke, the one for coming back from the Spire, and Kindleby sees what the ending made of the night.

kindleby_midwinter.description: The dark ending's first ask (Day 97): Tobin asks whether the Wakebearer will carry the ember round to Kindleby first at midwinter. '' (not asked, or another ending), 'first' (Kindleby first: it has waited longest) or 'ring' (round the way the light goes, from the Gull). Future: the midwinter round.

saltmarrow_homecoming_seen.description: The epilogue on Saltmarrow (Day 98, arrival event saltmarrow_homecoming): the Mercy puts in past the breakwater after the ending, the green lantern still on the dock-post; Mara sees what the ending made of the night (lit: the Spire a gold point over the lofts, the boats out; released: somebody sitting up at the Gull, the step warm; dark: the midwinter round, Saltmarrow writes its own list).

saltmarrow_aldous_after_seen.description: Told Aldous the Long Book's shut (Day 98, the epilogue, one-time): per ending, Oriel's name, the seventh novice, the brazier and the door-warden's answer to the Provost.

saltmarrow_aldous_heard_oriel.description: Told Aldous of the High Keeper after the ending (Day 98): Oriel Sayre signed the Long Book (climb/own) — he says her name for the first time — or sits in a boat that never went out (boat).

saltmarrow_aldous_knows_novice.description: Told Aldous the Wakebearer was the seventh novice on the east landing (Day 98; released or dark, once Oriel knows). He still can't find the face, and takes their word over his eyes.

saltmarrow_brazier_lit.description: The dark ending's homecoming (Day 98): the Wakebearer held the ember to the Wrens' brazier, laid for whoever comes down the stair, and it burns for the first time since the Snuffing (brazier_lit, a small fire light).

saltmarrow_aldous_crossing.description: The door-warden's answer to the Provost, kept (Day 98; needs saltmarrow_aldous_boat=letter): '' (not said), 'now' (lit or released: 'it's one or the other' — he'll cross and pay twice) or 'midwinter' (dark: he'll come with the ember on the round, carrying nothing). Future: Aldous on the Mercy.

thornwold_homecoming_seen.description: The epilogue on Thornwold (Day 99, arrival event thornwold_homecoming): the Mercy puts in at the lumber camp after the ending; Bram sees what the ending made of the night (lit: the Spire a gold point east past the cove's point, and he's stopped notching it; released: two at the Ridge Light's bench of a night, the far end warm; dark: a WINTER row cut on the tally board for what Thornwold would give at midwinter). Pell, if landed, per ending.

thornwold_bram_cut_row.description: Told Bram 'It took me first' in the lit ending's homecoming (Day 99): he cuts the Wakebearer a row on the tally board, not to count — a place on the board that's theirs.

thornwold_aldous_landed.description: Aldous kept the door-warden's answer (saltmarrow_aldous_crossing=now) and, knowing Wynn Sallow lives, came ashore at Thornwold off the Mercy and went up to the ridge (Day 99; in the homecoming, or the thornwold_aldous_ashore event if that was already seen). Moves Aldous off his Saltmarrow bench onto the Ridge Light's lantern bench.

thornwold_aldous_met_wynn.description: The two keepers on the ridge (Day 99, ridge arrival event thornwold_two_keepers): Aldous's sorry said in person; 'A door-warden isn't the door', said on the day the lanes run with nobody counting.

thornwold_last_coal_out.description: The last of the Spire's midwinter coal in the Lamp's iron box let go out, with Aldous watching (Day 99, lit or released: nothing left for it to keep). Future: the box empty on the bench.
